title: Autorepairlet: Safe-mode execution and versioned playbooks for low-blast remediation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an 'autorepairlet' runtime mode that allows ops runbook steps to execute in a constrained safe-mode: versioned playbooks, dry-run toggles, staged side-effecting step gating, and automatic revert/failover hooks. This ticket covers the server-side orchestration, RBAC checks, audit logging, and telemetry hooks needed to run remediation runlets with an explicit safe execution envelope so oncall can safely triage and apply fixes with minimal blast radius.
acceptance_criteria: Autorepairlet runtime exposes a 'safe_mode' boolean for any runbook execution request
Playbooks can be pinned by semantic version (v1.2.3) and executions log which playbook version ran
Side-effecting steps support 'dry_run' and 'canary_percent' parameters; when dry_run=true no state changes occur
Audit log entries are written to the central ops-audit stream (with actor, playbook_version, inputs, outcome) for all executions
RBAC: only users with 'ops:run-safemode' permission can execute non-dry runs; requests without permission are rejected with 403
Telemetry: per-step latency, success/failure, and revert-execution metrics show up in Console within 15 minutes
Playback/simulation harness can deterministically replay a previous execution with recorded inputs and produce the same decision path in dry-run mode
Automated rollback hook runs when a step marked 'revert_on_error' fails; revert is recorded and surfaced in the UI
technical_notes: Server: extend runlet-executor API with fields {safe_mode:boolean, playbook_version:string, dry_run:boolean, canary_percent:int}
Executor will short-circuit calls to effectful providers (k8s, infra, DB) when dry_run=true; instead, emit 'simulated' events to the audit stream
Introduce a lightweight semantic version resolver that resolves 'latest-stable' to a specific git tag/artifact id to ensure reproducibility
Persist execution manifests to the executions DB (playbook_version, inputs, computed decisions, step outcomes) to enable deterministic replay
Telemetry: emit OTLP spans per step with attributes for safe_mode/dry_run and correlate with execution_id and actor
RBAC: wire to existing SSO service and a new 'ops:run-safemode' permission controlled by org-admins
Encryption: any secrets used by steps must be fetched via KMS with auditable key usage; do not allow embedded plain-text creds in playbooks
Testing: use the synthetic-runbook simulator (ENG-834207) to validate behavior under failure modes
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Spike completed — prototype executor toggles dry_run and emits simulated events. Recorded replay path works for simple two-step playbook (A -> B).
2026-02-28: Design review with Security and Platform. Agreed on mandatory KMS retrieval for secret steps, and audit stream schema v2. Security requested threat model doc.
2026-03-03: Schema for executions DB drafted; added fields for playbook_version and canary_percent. Created RFC 'playbook-versioning-and-replay-2026-02' in Confluence.
2026-03-07: Implemented RBAC check hook and preliminary Console feature flag to show safe_mode executions in the UI. Integration tests wired to sandbox KMS key.
2026-03-10: Canary gating and automated revert prototype merged to branch feature/autorepairlet-safe-mode. Need PR for audit-stream schema migration and ops-audit consumer update.
2026-03-10: Blocker discovered — provider adapters still perform write calls in some edge paths; added ticket ENG-770124 to harden adapters for dry-run enforcement.
test_plan: Unit tests for executor flag branching (dry_run vs real) with mocked provider adapters
Integration test: run synthetic three-step playbook in sandbox cluster with dry_run=true and assert no external writes
Replay test: re-run an archived execution in simulation and compare decision path hashes
Chaos test: during canary (canary_percent=10) simulate step failure and assert revert hook triggers and audit shows revert outcome
Security review checklist completed: KMS usage verified, RBAC enforced, audit stream includes actor and request origin
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Internal beta): Enable safe_mode for 5% of internal runs, UI flag hidden; monitor telemetry for false positives — target SLO: zero unintended writes
Phase 2 (Oncall opt-in): Allow orgs with >1 oncall trained to opt in; surface playbook_version pinning in Console; run scheduled training session
Phase 3 (Default for newer playbooks): New playbooks default to safe_mode=true for first 7 days post-publish; after telemetry validation they can be promoted
Rollback: feature flag to disable execute-on-write at runtime; maintain manual intervention runbook for emergency disable
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Dry-run enforcement gaps in third-party adapters could still cause writes. Mitigation: Add adapter conformance tests and kill-switch that blocks any outbound write RPC from the executor process when safe_mode active.
Risk: Playbook version resolution drift could cause different behavior when replaying older runs. Mitigation: Persist artifact hashes and add an immutability policy for published playbook artifacts.

Risk: Operator confusion about safe_mode semantics. Mitigation: UX copy, in-console badges (DRY-RUN) and mandatory training + a 'simulate' button that shows step-by-step decision tree before execution.
Risk: Audit data volume spike. Mitigation: Downsample simulated events while retaining full decision-path metadata; stream full payloads to cold storage for 90 days.
